# Phase 5 evaluation (generated by scripts/evaluate_planner.py)

Simulation result on a synthetic box. Not real-world evidence.

All money values, probabilities, delays and thresholds are illustrative placeholders, not sourced [SOURCE NEEDED] (config/planner.yaml). The planner recommends; it never executes; final authority stays with QA. It is only as good as the potency estimate and the single-node thermal twin (which Phase 3C showed cannot represent a box with a payload; a richer twin, Phase 3D, is on the backlog), and it is NOT validated against real decisions.

## 1. The oracle (master brief section 3.5, V = 50,000, alpha = 0.95)

| action | cost | failure prob | expected loss | CVaR 0.95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| continue | 0 | 8% | 4,000 | 50,000 |
| reroute | 5,000 | 0.5% | 5,250 | 10,000 |

Exact (analytic) values; the expected-loss-optimal action is continue and the CVaR-optimal action is reroute.

## 2. The six demo scenarios at their checkpoints

Seed 20261021, 5000 scenarios per action, alpha 0.95, V 50,000, beta 200 per hour, V_thr 20,000, confidence gap threshold 10,000. The scheduled remaining time is the rest of the recording.

| scenario | hour | potency now | trust | verdict | CVaR-optimal | expected-optimal | disagree | continue fails | VaR (chosen) | CVaR - mean (chosen) | route | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline_ok | 24 | 99.97% | trusted | ok | continue | continue | no | 0.0% | 865 | 728 | auto_approved | active |
| door_open_excursion | 12 | 99.96% | trusted | ok | continue | continue | no | 0.0% | 865 | 728 | auto_approved | active |
| reefer_failure | 20 | 99.28% | trusted | thermal_anomaly | reroute_to_depot | reroute_to_depot | no | 78.6% | 7,400 | 190 | auto_approved | active |
| heatwave_transit | 40 | 99.72% | trusted | thermal_anomaly | reroute_to_depot | reroute_to_depot | no | 78.5% | 7,400 | 0 | auto_approved | active |
| spoof_attempt | 20 | 99.95% | untrusted | suspected_falsification | continue | continue | no | 0.0% | 865 | 728 | needs_human | quarantined_pending_review |
| hidden_spoilage | 50 | 99.92% | untrusted | suspected_falsification | continue | re_source | yes | 100.0% | 50,865 | 728 | needs_human | quarantined_pending_review |

Why, in plain words:

- **baseline_ok** (hour 24): continuing fails in 0.0 percent of scenarios. Route: auto_approved.
- **door_open_excursion** (hour 12): continuing fails in 0.0 percent of scenarios. Route: auto_approved.
- **reefer_failure** (hour 20): continuing would fail in 78.6 percent of scenarios (bad-case loss 50,980); reroute_to_depot has bad-case loss 7,600. Route: auto_approved.
- **heatwave_transit** (hour 40): continuing would fail in 78.5 percent of scenarios (bad-case loss 50,980); reroute_to_depot has bad-case loss 7,400. Route: auto_approved.
- **spoof_attempt** (hour 20): the readings are untrusted, so the plan starts from the worst-case bound (tau_eq 590 h instead of 41 h); continuing fails in 0.0 percent of scenarios. Route: needs_human.
- **hidden_spoilage** (hour 50): the readings are untrusted, so the plan starts from the worst-case bound (tau_eq 23,240 h instead of 68 h); continuing fails in 100 percent of scenarios, but so does every cheaper-than-replacement action, and continuing is the cheapest. Route: needs_human.

### Cases where the planner looks odd (reported, not hidden)

- `spoof_attempt` and `hidden_spoilage` are untrusted, so the plan starts from the worst-case bound, which assumes no cooling after the doubt began. Almost every action then fails in nearly every scenario, and the recommendation falls to whichever action is cheapest or starts fresh (re_source). A person must decide in both cases; the recommendation is a pointer, not an answer.
- In an untrusted case `continue` can be recommended although it fails in nearly every scenario: when every in-box action fails, the cheapest one has the smallest loss. The route is needs_human, which is the intended safeguard.
- The first run of this evaluation showed a flaw that was fixed (decision 0009, P5 and P6): at hour 20 of `reefer_failure` (cooling already short of its job) the planner gave 0 percent failure for `continue` because it assumed working cooling and a cool ambient. Section 3 shows the effect of each fix.

## 3. What the two modelling fixes change

| scenario | model | continue fails | continue CVaR | CVaR-optimal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reefer_failure | as shipped (anomaly handling on, persistence forecast) | 78.6% | 50,980 | reroute_to_depot |
| reefer_failure | no anomaly handling (P5 off) | 0.0% | 1,012 | continue |
| reefer_failure | fixed 22 degree ambient forecast (P6 off) | 0.0% | 1,012 | continue |
| reefer_failure | both off (the first version) | 0.0% | 1,012 | continue |
| heatwave_transit | as shipped (anomaly handling on, persistence forecast) | 78.5% | 50,980 | reroute_to_depot |
| heatwave_transit | no anomaly handling (P5 off) | 0.0% | 1,012 | continue |
| heatwave_transit | fixed 22 degree ambient forecast (P6 off) | 0.0% | 1,012 | continue |
| heatwave_transit | both off (the first version) | 0.0% | 1,012 | continue |

For reference, the recording of `reefer_failure` ends at about 86 percent potency (below the 90 percent limit) and `heatwave_transit` ends above it: the ambient is 41 to 48 degrees in both after the checkpoint. These recordings are one simulated path each, not a test of the planner's probabilities.

## 5. Stability across seeds

The same decision with the configured seed (20261021) and nine other seeds. A recommendation that changes with the seed is a near-tie that sampling noise can flip (the CVaR of an action with rare failures rests on few scenarios).

| scenario | hour | CVaR-optimal over 10 seeds | stable |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline_ok | 24 | continue 10 of 10 | stable |
| door_open_excursion | 12 | continue 10 of 10 | stable |
| reefer_failure | 20 | reroute_to_depot 10 of 10 | stable |
| heatwave_transit | 40 | reroute_to_depot 10 of 10 | stable |
| spoof_attempt | 20 | continue 10 of 10 | stable |
| hidden_spoilage | 50 | continue 5 of 10, re_source 5 of 10 | VARIES WITH THE SEED |

## 6. What this does and does not show

- It shows that the pieces fit together: the planner reads the existing potency, trust and bound outputs, never starts from a point estimate when the readings are in doubt, sends doubtful cases to a person, and logs every decision in a signed, hash-chained log.
- It does not show that the recommendations are right. The costs, V, beta, delays, cooling failure chances, ambient forecast and thresholds are placeholders; the sensitivity table shows the recommendation moves with them.
- The thermal twin is a single-node model; on a box with a payload (Phase 3C) it is wrong in known ways. The persistence ambient forecast cannot foresee a change in the weather.
- Signing protects records after signing; it does not stop a lie at the sensor (A18). The planner therefore uses the physics-based trust level, not the signature, to decide whether a reading may drive a decision.

Simulation result on a synthetic box. Not real-world evidence.
